articles.title: Arunachal's Border Villages Hoist Tiranga at China Frontier as India Marks 80th Independence Day
articles.excerpt: Students, soldiers, and villagers in Arunachal Pradesh's Tawang district unfurled the national flag at border outposts and frontier villages, reinforcing India's sovereignty claims in territory that China disputes.
articles.image_caption: The Indian tricolor flies at a border outpost in Arunachal Pradesh's Tawang district. Frontier villages near the China border celebrated India's 80th Independence Day with flag hoisting ceremonies.
articles.nri_angle: The border tensions in Arunachal Pradesh resonate with the Indian diaspora tracking sovereignty issues, while the US recognition of Arunachal as Indian territory adds a geopolitical dimension relevant to NRIs in America.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: US Leaders and Diaspora Mark India's 80th Independence Day With Parades and Proclamations
articles.excerpt: Massachusetts declared August 15 as 'India Day,' while community celebrations from San Jose to New York honor the dual milestone of India at 80 and America at 250.
articles.image_caption: Indian-American community leaders at the Consulate General of India in New York during the Azadi Ka Mahotsav curtain raiser. Celebrations across the U.S. mark India's 80th Independence Day and America's 250th anniversary.
articles.nri_angle: Indian Americans across the U.S. are celebrating India's 80th Independence Day with parades, proclamations, and community events, with Massachusetts officially declaring August 15 as India Day.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Nana Patekar's Decade-Long Fight for India's Farmers Earns Unlikely Political Praise
articles.excerpt: The veteran Bollywood actor, who founded NAAM Foundation in 2015 after witnessing farmer suicides in Maharashtra, has emerged as a rare non-partisan voice on agrarian distress — and recently partnered with the UP government on a viral cyber awareness campaign.
articles.image_caption: Nana Patekar during a visit to drought-affected farmers in Maharashtra. The veteran actor co-founded NAAM Foundation in 2015 to support families of farmers who died by suicide.
articles.nri_angle: Patekar's farmer advocacy resonates with the Indian diaspora concerned about agrarian distress back home, while his cyber awareness campaign highlights scam risks that also affect NRIs.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Liverpool Sells Stake to Bezos-Backed Consortium Led by British-Indian Businessman Amit Bhatia
articles.excerpt: A group including Amazon's Jeff Bezos and the Mittal family will acquire roughly 30% of Liverpool FC in a deal valuing the club at £5.5 billion, with Bhatia becoming vice-chairman.
articles.image_caption: Liverpool FC's Anfield stadium in Liverpool, England. British-Indian businessman Amit Bhatia is leading a consortium backed by Jeff Bezos to acquire a stake in the Premier League club.
articles.nri_angle: British-Indian businessman Amit Bhatia and the Mittal Family Trusts take a leading stake in one of English football's most iconic clubs, marking another milestone for Indian capital in global sports.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: U.S. Calls India a 'Critical Power' After Dropping 'Indo' From Pacific Command Name
articles.excerpt: A senior Pentagon official pushed back against concerns that renaming INDOPACOM to PACOM signals diminished attention to India, calling the U.S.-India relationship 'vital' with 'natural partnership' potential.
articles.nri_angle: The U.S.-India strategic relationship directly affects millions of Indian Americans and NRIs through defence ties, diplomatic standing, and the broader geopolitical environment in which the diaspora operates.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: From Amritsar's Streets to TIME100: Vikas Khanna's Journey to Global Culinary Stardom
articles.excerpt: Born with clubfoot and bullied as a child, the Michelin-starred chef built a culinary empire in New York, earned a TIME100 honor in 2026, and is now redefining Indian cuisine on the world stage through his restaurant Bungalow.
articles.nri_angle: Khanna's journey from Amritsar to Michelin stardom and the TIME100 list embodies the Indian diaspora experience of overcoming adversity abroad while staying rooted in Indian identity and culture.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Seven Indian American Women Named to Forbes' 50 Over 50 List
articles.excerpt: From the CEO of a $26 billion manufacturing company to the co-founder of Stop AAPI Hate, Indian American women are well represented on Forbes' annual list of entrepreneurs and changemakers over 50.
articles.image_caption: Jayshree Ullal, CEO of Arista Networks, is among seven Indian American women featured on the Forbes 50 Over 50 list. Ullal is one of America's wealthiest female executives.
articles.nri_angle: The strong showing of Indian American women across entrepreneurship and social impact on a premier business list underscores the community's expanding influence beyond technology into manufacturing, finance, spirits, and social advocacy.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Gen Z Professional Turns Down ₹1 Crore Job Offer at 25 Over Toxic Workplace Concerns
articles.excerpt: A 25-year-old's decision to walk away from a high-paying role has gone viral on LinkedIn, reigniting the debate over work-life balance and India's corporate hustle culture.
articles.image_caption: A young professional works at a laptop in a modern office setting. A 25-year-old Gen Z candidate's decision to reject a high-paying job over workplace culture concerns has gone viral on Indian social media.
articles.nri_angle: The debate over India's corporate hustle culture resonates strongly with NRI professionals who often cite work-life balance differences as a factor in their decision to work abroad.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Attacks on Indians Abroad Surged From 29 to Over 100 a Year in Five Years, MEA Data Shows
articles.excerpt: Ministry of External Affairs data tabled in Parliament reveals the US recorded the highest number of attacks on Indian nationals from 2021 to 2025, with Ireland and the UK emerging as new hotspots.
articles.nri_angle: MEA data shows Indian nationals in the US, UK, Canada, and Ireland face a sharp increase in racially motivated attacks, with Indian students bearing a disproportionate burden of fatalities.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Pew Survey Across 36 Nations Reveals How the World Views India — and Its Rivalry With Pakistan
articles.excerpt: A Pew Research Center survey of 42,151 people in 36 countries finds India viewed favorably in most nations, while Indians and Pakistanis continue to see each other as their greatest threat.
articles.nri_angle: Favorable global views of India correlate with warmer attitudes toward diaspora communities, while India-Pakistan hostility documented in the survey mirrors tensions in diaspora settings.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: SAD Demands CBI Probe Into Attack on Sukhbir Badal, Alleges Conspiracy Against Moderate Leadership
articles.excerpt: The Shiromani Akali Dal seeks a high court-monitored investigation, while PM Modi's call to Harsimrat Kaur Badal draws cross-party attention to the security situation in Punjab.
articles.nri_angle: The attack on the Akali Dal president directly concerns the global Sikh diaspora, which maintains strong ties with Punjab's political and religious institutions, particularly in the US, Canada, and UK.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Bhagwa Dhwaj vs Tricolour: India's Independence Day Celebrations Hit by BJP-Congress Flag Wars
articles.excerpt: As BJP launches its fourth Har Ghar Tiranga campaign, opposition leaders question why the RSS took 52 years to hoist the national flag at its Nagpur headquarters.
articles.nri_angle: Independence Day is one of the most widely celebrated events for NRIs, making the political fight over the Tricolour directly relevant to diaspora Indians who observe August 15 as a cultural and national identity marker.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Farage Faces Count Binface as Clacton By-Election Becomes Britain's Most Surreal Political Contest
articles.excerpt: After resigning amid a financial scandal, the Reform UK leader triggered a by-election that all major parties boycotted — leaving a novelty candidate in a bin costume as his primary opponent.
articles.nri_angle: Reform UK's anti-immigration stance and financial transparency concerns relevant to British Indian communities
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: CJP Launches 'School Thik Karo' Campaign to Fix Rural Government Schools
articles.excerpt: The Cockroach Janta Party has announced a nationwide citizen-led campaign to audit and improve infrastructure in rural government schools, deploying community volunteers to assess electricity, water, sanitation, and mid-day meal quality.
articles.image_caption: CJP has launched a nationwide campaign to audit and improve rural government schools across India.
articles.nri_angle: CJP's shift from exam protests to grassroots education reform signals a maturing youth movement with implications for India's broader governance and the diaspora's engagement with homeland issues.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Amaravati Takes Shape as India's Newest Capital With Rs 56,000 Crore Push
articles.excerpt: Andhra Pradesh's greenfield capital city is rising from farmland with massive infrastructure investment, Singapore partnership, and a legally cemented status as the state's sole capital — targeting completion by March 2028.
articles.image_caption: Andhra Pradesh has launched Rs 56,000 crore in projects for its greenfield capital Amaravati, with tenders issued and 74 construction works underway.
articles.nri_angle: Amaravati's development has drawn significant NRI investment interest, particularly from Telugu diaspora communities who see opportunities in the capital region's real estate and technology sectors.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Delaware Declares August 15 India Day, Joining Growing Wave of US State Proclamations
articles.excerpt: The First State becomes the latest to formally recognize India's Independence Day, reflecting the Indian American community's growing civic influence across the United States.
articles.nri_angle: Indian Americans in Delaware and across the US are gaining formal civic recognition through India Day proclamations, reflecting the community's growing political influence.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Tata Sons AGM Faces Quorum Hurdle as Charity Commissioner Bars Trust Meetings
articles.excerpt: A regulatory freeze on the Sir Ratan Tata Trust has blocked it from nominating a representative required for a valid shareholder vote at the August 18 annual general meeting.
articles.nri_angle: The Tata Group's global operations, including Jaguar Land Rover, TCS, and Tata Steel Europe, could see delayed strategic decisions as the governance crisis prevents key funding and board composition discussions.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Mamata Banerjee Calls Delimitation BJP's Tool to Divide Bengal and India
articles.excerpt: West Bengal CM attacks Centre's plan to expand Lok Sabha to 850 seats, warns NRC and detention camps will follow
articles.image_caption: West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee has accused the BJP of using the Delimitation Bill as a tool to divide Bengal and India along political lines.
articles.nri_angle: For NRIs with roots in West Bengal, the delimitation debate carries significant implications for home-state representation and the broader trajectory of Indian federalism.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: 90,000 London Professional Jobs Forecast to Move to UK Regions by 2031
articles.excerpt: Analysis by Robert Walters projects a £9 billion boost to regional economies as bankers, lawyers and accountants leave the capital amid rising costs and devolution push
articles.nri_angle: Thousands of Indian-origin professionals work in London's financial and legal sectors. This shift could reshape career opportunities, living costs, and visa sponsorship patterns for the UK's Indian community.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Jr NTR Undergoes Successful Shoulder Surgery at KIMS Hyderabad
articles.excerpt: The Dragon star's arthroscopic procedure at KIMS Hospitals follows a shoulder injury sustained during filming in late July
articles.nri_angle: Jr NTR has a massive following among the Telugu diaspora worldwide, with Dragon being one of the most anticipated pan-Indian films for NRI audiences.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian-Origin Teen in Massachusetts Charged With Killing Mother and Brother, Used ChatGPT to Script Family Killings
articles.excerpt: Arjun Aravind, a high school student in Acton, Massachusetts, allegedly killed his mother Sudha Venkatesan and 14-year-old brother before fleeing in the family car.
articles.image_caption: Arjun Aravind, an Indian-origin teenager from Acton, Massachusetts, faces two murder charges after the deaths of his mother and younger brother.
articles.nri_angle: The killing of an Indian-origin mother and her 14-year-old son in a quiet Massachusetts suburb, allegedly by her own teen who used ChatGPT to fantasize about the act, has shaken the local Indian-American community in Acton.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Army Veteran Demands Netflix Pull Operation Safed Sagar Over Flag Code Breach in Coffin Scene
articles.excerpt: A retired Indian Army officer has called for the suspension of the widely praised Kargil War series after spotting an incorrect draping of the Tricolour on a martyr's coffin.
articles.nri_angle: The controversy over Netflix's globally available Kargil War series resonates with diaspora viewers who watched it with patriotic pride and now face the debate over balancing accountability for flag code errors with supporting military tributes.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: California Uber and Lyft Drivers Take Historic Step Toward Unionization
articles.excerpt: The California Gig Workers Union has filed a petition to represent over 800,000 rideshare drivers, backed by tens of thousands of signatures, in what could become the largest expansion of private-sector collective bargaining in state history.
articles.nri_angle: South Asian and Indian-origin immigrants make up a significant share of California's rideshare workforce, particularly in the Bay Area, Sacramento, and Los Angeles. The unionization effort could reshape wages and job protections for these drivers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Pravasi Trust Urges Kerala to Tap NRI Savings for High-Speed Rail Project
articles.excerpt: A Pravasi trust has submitted a memorandum to Kerala Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan proposing tax-free bonds to channel Non-Resident Keralite savings toward a high-speed railway linking Thiruvananthapuram and Kasaragod.
articles.nri_angle: Directly proposes channeling NRI savings into Kerala infrastructure, offering diaspora Keralites a government-backed investment tied to their home state's development.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: UK MP Dhesi Presses Punjab Officials on NRI Land Disputes and Air Connectivity
articles.excerpt: British MP Tanmanjeet Singh Dhesi met Punjab's NRI affairs minister to push for a one-window grievance system, direct flights to Amritsar and Chandigarh, and reopening of the Kartarpur Sahib Corridor.
articles.nri_angle: Directly addresses NRI concerns including property disputes, extortion, and connectivity for the large UK-based Punjabi community.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: UK PM Burnham Taps Indian-Origin BBC Strategist as Downing Street Advisor
articles.excerpt: Gautam Rangarajan, who spent over two decades at the BBC rising to Group Director of Strategy, has been appointed expert adviser on structure and process at 10 Downing Street.
articles.image_caption: The entrance to 10 Downing Street in London. UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has appointed Gautam Rangarajan, a former senior BBC executive, as his adviser on government operations.
articles.nri_angle: Rangarajan's appointment adds to a growing cohort of Indian-origin figures in senior UK government roles under Prime Minister Burnham, including AI Minister Kanishka Narayan.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Stanford Professor Easha Anand Elected to American Law Institute
articles.excerpt: The Indian-American law professor and Supreme Court litigator joins the prestigious legal body that has shaped American law for nearly a century.
articles.nri_angle: An Indian-American law professor who grew up partly in India has been elected to one of the most prestigious legal organizations in the United States, reflecting the growing influence of Indian-origin legal scholars at the highest levels of American jurisprudence.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Police Fire Tear Gas on Jharkhand Student Marchers as Ex-JPSC Chief Arrested
articles.excerpt: A two-week protest over alleged exam fraud erupts into violent clashes at the state assembly, forcing government concessions and political intervention.
articles.nri_angle: The examination fraud crisis reflects systemic issues in India's public sector recruitment that contribute to skilled professionals seeking opportunities abroad.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's UPI Reaches 10 Countries as Diaspora Emerges as Key Driver of Global Payments Push
articles.excerpt: From Greece to the Gulf, India's homegrown payment system is expanding rapidly — and the 32-million-strong diaspora is at the center of the strategy.
articles.image_caption: YouTube / The Indian Express
articles.nri_angle: UPI's global expansion directly benefits NRIs by slashing remittance costs and enabling instant cross-border payments in countries where millions of Indians live, work, and study.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Nearly ₹1 Lakh Crore in Bank Deposits Lie Unclaimed in India as RBI Pushes Recovery Drive
articles.excerpt: Unclaimed deposits with RBI's fund have surged to ₹86,917 crore, prompting a nationwide campaign and a centralized portal to help depositors and their heirs reclaim forgotten money.
articles.nri_angle: NRIs who have left bank accounts dormant in India after moving abroad are among those most likely to have unclaimed deposits; the UDGAM portal and new claim processes offer a way to search for and recover this money remotely.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: PM Modi Tells Youth to Read Autobiographies, Warns Against Shortcut Culture at Kovind Book Launch
articles.excerpt: At the release of former President Ram Nath Kovind's autobiography, Modi urged young people to find inspiration in real life stories instead of social media reels, saying "shortcuts will cut you short."
articles.nri_angle: Modi's message against shortcut culture and emphasis on reading resonates with diaspora families who value education and self-improvement, while Kovind's journey from a marginalized background to India's presidency is a story that inspires communities worldwide.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: University of Michigan Drops First-Semester Grades for Freshmen Citing Mental Health Crisis
articles.excerpt: The university's largest college will replace letter grades with pass/no credit for incoming freshmen starting fall 2027, joining a growing number of elite schools rethinking academic pressure.
articles.nri_angle: The policy directly affects thousands of Indian-American students and families who make up a significant portion of U-M's undergraduate population, one of the largest groups of international and diaspora students at any U.S. public university.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Sourav Ganguly and Wife Dona File Police Complaint After Six Months of Death Threat Letters
articles.excerpt: The former India captain lodged a formal complaint in Kolkata after couriered letters escalated from fan mail to explicit threats against his family.
articles.nri_angle: Sourav Ganguly is one of the most recognizable Indian sports figures globally, and threats against him and his family are of direct concern to the Indian diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian Chemist Gautam Desiraju Wins Crystallography's Highest Honor, the Ewald Prize
articles.excerpt: The IISc professor emeritus and grandson of India's second President is recognized for pioneering crystal engineering over a five-decade career.
articles.image_caption: Gautam R. Desiraju, professor emeritus at the Indian Institute of Science in Bengaluru. He has been awarded the 14th Ewald Prize for his foundational work in crystal engineering.
articles.nri_angle: Desiraju earned his PhD at the University of Illinois and conducted research at Eastman Kodak before returning to India, embodying the diaspora-to-homeland knowledge pipeline.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Michigan Indian Americans Honor Padma Shri Recipient Stephen Knapp at IHPC 2026
articles.excerpt: The India Heritage Preservation Council celebrated the American author and Vedic scholar who spent over 40 years studying and promoting Indian spiritual heritage.
articles.image_caption: Stephen Knapp, also known as Sri Nandanandana Dasa, is an American author and Vedic scholar. He was awarded the Padma Shri in January 2025 for his contributions to literature and education.
articles.nri_angle: The event highlights how Indian American community organizations actively honor non-Indian allies who champion Hindu heritage in the United States.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Naval Chief Visits Mauritius as Defence Outreach to Africa Expands
articles.excerpt: Admiral Krishna Swaminathan's four-day trip and an Indian Army contingent's march in Côte d'Ivoire's Independence Day parade mark New Delhi's growing military footprint across Africa.
articles.image_caption: Chief of Naval Staff Admiral Krishna Swaminathan during his visit to Mauritius for maritime security talks. The visit is part of India's expanding defence outreach across the Indian Ocean and Africa.
articles.nri_angle: Mauritius has the largest proportional Indian-origin population of any country, with roughly two-thirds of its residents tracing ancestry to the subcontinent. India's defence outreach to Africa also extends a security umbrella to Indian diaspora communities across the continent.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian Universities Nearly Quintuple Presence in QS World Rankings Since 2015 as IIT Delhi Hits Record 118th
articles.excerpt: India now has 52 universities in the QS World Rankings, up from 11 a decade ago, with IIT Delhi achieving the highest position ever for an Indian institution.
articles.image_caption: IIT Delhi campus, India's highest-ranked university in the QS World Rankings 2027 at 118th globally. India now has 52 universities in the rankings, up from 11 in 2015.
articles.nri_angle: India's fivefold increase in globally ranked universities expands options for diaspora families considering Indian institutions and signals growing international recognition of Indian higher education.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Who Is Deepak Dhar? The Small-Town UP Boy Who Studied Under Feynman — and Just Joined Physics' Most Exclusive Club
articles.excerpt: The 74-year-old Indian theoretical physicist just won the 2026 Dirac Medal, becoming the first Indian-born recipient. His journey from Pratapgarh to Caltech to the pinnacle of world physics — and the sandpile that connects it all to AI.
articles.image_caption: Deepak Dhar, INSA Distinguished Professor at ICTS-TIFR Bengaluru. The 74-year-old theoretical physicist won the 2026 ICTP Dirac Medal for his contributions to statistical mechanics.

sources.label: IIT Kanpur - Prof Deepak Dhar Interview

articles.nri_angle: Deepak Dhar's journey from a small-town UP childhood to Caltech and back to India, winning honors that place him among Hawking and Witten, represents the deep scientific contributions of Indian-origin minds that often go uncelebrated compared to tech industry success stories.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: From Barren Land to Cricket's Premier Hub: How Jay Shah Built the BCCI Centre of Excellence
articles.excerpt: The 40-acre Bengaluru facility has drawn Hardik Pandya as its first permanent resident and Bangladesh's cricket board for a study visit, but a fitness communication breakdown has put its sports science operations under review.
articles.image_caption: The BCCI Centre of Excellence was inaugurated by Jay Shah and Roger Binny in Bengaluru in September 2024. The 40-acre facility has become central to Indian cricket training and rehabilitation operations.
articles.nri_angle: The BCCI Centre of Excellence represents India's biggest investment in cricket infrastructure, directly affecting how India's stars prepare for ICC events that diaspora fans follow closely, and drawing international study visits from Bangladesh.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Canadian Police Arrest Suspect Seven Months After Indian-Origin Woman Himanshi Khurana Murdered in Toronto
articles.excerpt: Abdul Ghafoori, 32, faces first-degree murder charges after a Canada-wide manhunt following the December 2025 killing classified as intimate partner violence.
articles.image_caption: Toronto Police had issued a Canada-wide warrant for Abdul Ghafoori after Himanshi Khurana was found dead in December 2025. Ghafoori has now been arrested approximately seven months later.
articles.nri_angle: The murder and subsequent manhunt highlighted safety concerns for Indian nationals in Canada and prompted diplomatic intervention from the Indian Consulate General in Toronto.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian Physicist Deepak Dhar Wins 2026 Dirac Medal, Joining Hawking and Witten in Elite Physics Pantheon
articles.excerpt: The IISER Pune professor becomes the first Indian-born scientist to receive the ICTP Dirac Medal, awarded alongside three co-laureates for pioneering work in statistical mechanics and AI.
articles.image_caption: Indian physicist Deepak Dhar, pictured alongside the ICTP Dirac Medal announcement. Dhar was awarded the 2026 medal for his pioneering contributions to statistical mechanics.
articles.nri_angle: Dhar is a rare example of a world-class theoretical physicist who built his entire career at Indian institutions, winning global recognition while working from TIFR, IISER Pune, and ICTS-TIFR Bengaluru.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ashna Tambe Becomes Penn's First Indian American Women's Basketball Player
articles.excerpt: The Texas guard, whose mother played at the national level in India, is combining Ivy League academics with a trailblazing basketball career at the University of Pennsylvania.
articles.image_caption: Ashna Tambe, a guard from Plano, Texas, joined the University of Pennsylvania women's basketball programme in 2024. She became the first Indian American player in Penn's women's basketball history.
articles.nri_angle: First Indian American player in Penn women's basketball history, trained by her mother who played national-level basketball in India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian-Origin Woman Wins £6.6 Million After 23-Year Divorce Battle Exposes Husband's Hidden Fortune
articles.excerpt: Varsha Gohil's two-decade fight against a husband who concealed £28 million has changed UK divorce law for women married to men who hide their wealth.
articles.image_caption: Varsha Gohil and Bhadresh Gohil pictured during their 23-year divorce battle in the UK. The case resulted in a £6.6 million settlement after the husband was convicted of hiding £28 million in assets.
articles.nri_angle: The case sets a UK legal precedent affecting NRIs in divorce disputes, establishing that hidden assets cannot shield wealth from fair division.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Modi Congratulates Vance on New Son as Leaders Review India-US Strategic Ties
articles.excerpt: The phone call covered trade, defense, and technology cooperation, with Modi extending personal congratulations on the birth of Alec Neel Vance — the first baby born to a sitting VP in 150 years.
articles.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Modi spoke with US Vice President JD Vance by phone on August 8, congratulating him on the birth of his son and reviewing progress on India-US strategic ties.
articles.nri_angle: The Modi-Vance relationship has personal significance for Indian Americans through Usha Vance's heritage, and the pending trade deal could affect visa and employment policies central to the diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Shrey Parikh Wins 2026 Scripps Spelling Bee as Indian Americans Claim 30th Title in 36 Years
articles.excerpt: The 14-year-old California eighth-grader set a new spell-off record with 32 words in 90 seconds, extending Indian American dominance at the nation's premier spelling competition.
articles.image_caption: Shrey Parikh celebrates his victory at the 98th Scripps National Spelling Bee in Washington, D.C. The 14-year-old from California set a new record by spelling 32 words in a 90-second spell-off.
articles.nri_angle: Indian Americans have won 30 of the last 36 Scripps National Spelling Bee championships, with the 2026 winner Shrey Parikh continuing a cultural legacy of competitive spelling excellence.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Falls Behind Turkey in the Fifth-Generation Fighter Jet Race
articles.excerpt: Turkey's KAAN fighter has completed ground tests of its second prototype, while India's AMCA programme is still years away from its first flight — but a private sector push could close the gap.
articles.image_caption: Turkey's KAAN fifth-generation fighter jet during testing. The programme has moved rapidly from maiden flight in 2024 to multiple prototype ground tests in 2026.
articles.nri_angle: India's defence self-reliance efforts, including the AMCA programme, are closely watched by the diaspora as markers of national technological progress. The private sector opening also creates potential opportunities for diaspora professionals in defence technology.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Pakistan's Fuel Crisis Deepens as IMF-Driven Price Hikes Spark Transport Strike Threats
articles.excerpt: Daily fuel price revisions, soaring diesel costs, and Middle East supply disruptions have pushed Pakistan's transport sector to the brink of a nationwide shutdown.
articles.image_caption: Pakistan moved to daily fuel price revisions under IMF conditions in July, triggering protests from transport operators.
articles.nri_angle: Pakistan's fuel crisis and potential transport shutdowns directly affect the South Asian region's economic stability. For Indian diaspora members with family ties to the subcontinent and business interests in cross-border trade, the crisis signals broader regional economic fragility.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Pakistan's System Has Collapsed, Says Interior Minister Naqvi, Fueling Coup Speculation
articles.excerpt: Speaking at the Pakistan Economic Summit, Mohsin Naqvi — Army Chief Asim Munir's closest political ally — warned that frustrated youth could "overturn everything," drawing comparisons to India's Cockroach Janta Party movement. The army distanced itself from his remarks.
articles.nri_angle: Pakistan's deepening governance crisis and coup speculation carry direct implications for India-Pakistan relations, regional stability, and the broader South Asian diaspora community.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Rishabh Pant Seeks Uttarakhand CM's Help to Buy Land, Build First Home in Native State
articles.excerpt: India cricketer made a late-night appeal on X to CM Pushkar Singh Dhami, saying he wants to move back from Delhi and buy land at government rates. Dhami responded with assurance of full support.
articles.nri_angle: Rishabh Pant, one of India's most globally recognized cricketers, seeks to return home to Uttarakhand — a story that resonates with NRIs navigating property ownership complexities in their native states.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
